$comment: Reference config for the Claude Code cloud environment this repo expects. Nothing consumes this file automatically — the environment is configured in the claude.ai/code UI — but it is the checked-in record of what that UI should say, so the next person (or session) doesn't rediscover it from proxy 403s. .claude/hooks/cloud-env-check.mjs compares this file against the live session at boot; run it with --verify-domains to probe the allowlist itself.
name: front-desk

handshake.note: cloud-env-check.mjs hashes this file's domains + env vars into a 12-hex digest; the dialog echoes it back via the variable named here, so a stale dialog is caught at boot instead of by a failed install. The variable's name is hashed (renaming it is a real dialog change); its value is excluded (it IS the digest). Run `node .claude/hooks/cloud-env-check.mjs --print-digest` for the current expected value. Another repo adopts the check by copying cloud-env-check.mjs + this block with its own variable/prefix — no script edits.

networkAccess.$comment: The default Trusted allowlist covers registry.npmjs.org but NOT JSR or DoltHub (verified 2026-07-27: both 403 through the proxy, killing npm install and the whole read plane). Hence custom. Wildcard entries carry a 'probe' host so --verify-domains can test them.

allowedDomains.reason: JSR npm-compat registry — the @bounded-systems/* deps (guest-room, verbspec, verbspec-mcp) resolve here, not npmjs
read plane: www.dolthub.com (public SQL API) + doltremoteapi.dolthub.com (dolt clone/push)
apex, in case a redirect lands on it
deno install — `deno check` is this repo's type gate

Lean toolchain downloads, historical origin. An earlier note here asserted singular-is-correct 'verified via strings on the binary' — but on 2026-07-31 a live `lake build` watched elan request https://releases.lean-lang.org/lean4/v4.32.2/lean-4.32.2-linux.tar.zst (PLURAL) and take a proxy 403, so current elan resolves the plural host and this entry alone no longer provisions a toolchain. Keep both entries until confirmed which the shipping elan uses; the empirical check below is the tiebreaker, and it disagreed with the strings-based one

Lean toolchain downloads, the origin current elan actually requests (observed 2026-07-31, see previous entry). NOT YET ALLOWLISTED in the environment UI as of that date — adding it there is the action; this entry records the requirement

The OSV API — the advisory database the shared scanning lane actually gates on. Probed 2026-07-31 → 404 (reachable; a blocked host yields 000); it was blocked on 2026-07-30, so it reached the dialog in between and was never recorded here. This repo needs it specifically: deno.lock is converted to CycloneDX for scanning (ci-workflows#1), which took the scanned surface from 33 to 136 packages, and none of those advisories can be checked from a session without this host. Query the gating source rather than a second tool's opinion: POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query -d '{"package":{"name":"X","ecosystem":"npm"},"version":"Y"}' and read affected[].ranges[].events[].fixed.
nvm downloads, if a newer Node than the image's 22.x is ever wanted (engines floor is 22.18)
the claim plane — FDS_CLAIM_ENDPOINT points here; src/lease-client.ts is dead without it (this host was silently dropped once when the broker was added; --verify-domains exists to catch exactly that)
OIDC token broker for credentialed mirror writes (docs/write-surfaces.md)

setupScriptNote: Deliberately empty: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (repo-versioned, reviewed) is the single source of provisioning truth. Optionally pre-warm the repo-independent toolchains (dolt/deno/elan) here for faster first boot; the hook no-ops over anything already present.
knownCaveats: Secrets never go in environmentVariables — the dialog stores them account-visible in plaintext. Credentialed writes go through the mirror-migrate workflow_dispatch + OIDC broker instead (docs/write-surfaces.md).

Environment VARIABLES freeze at session start — dialog edits reach only NEW sessions. Domain allowlist edits apply LIVE to running sessions. Both verified empirically 2026-07-30; this asymmetry explains most 'the dialog says X but the session sees Y' confusion.

Environment VARIABLES are scoped to the ENVIRONMENT, not to a repo: a session on a DIFFERENT repository that uses this environment still inherits FDS_READS, FDS_CLAIM_ENDPOINT and FDS_ENV_CONFIG — with no cloud-env-check.mjs present to interpret them. So the handshake variable being set does NOT mean the session is in this repo. Verified 2026-07-30 the expensive way: a session on bounded-systems/infra saw FDS_ENV_CONFIG=eb77de38c2bb, found no .claude/cloud-environment.json, confirmed `git log --all -- .claude` was empty, and concluded the hook had never existed on any branch — all of it accurate about infra and none of it about this repo. Before concluding the record is missing, check WHICH repo the session is in.

The GitHub proxy limits release-asset downloads to session-attached repositories regardless of network level, so the dolt install (a dolthub/dolt release asset) can 403 even with these domains. Fallback: the dolthub/dolt Docker image — Docker Hub is on the default Trusted list (docker/dolt-server/).
The cloud image ships Node 22.x; engines.node is >=22.18 (native TS type-stripping floor). Suite verified 40/40 on 22.22.2.

elan resolves toolchains from release.lean-lang.org but falls back to github.com/leanprover/lean4/releases/download/... for some assets, which is subject to the session-attached-repo limit above. So the elan.lean-lang.org + release.lean-lang.org pair gets the elan binary and should get the toolchain, but Lean provisioning is the one step still worth confirming empirically after an environment edit — `elan toolchain install stable` is the check.

Scope every repo the queue might surface AT SESSION CREATION. Attaching one mid-session goes through an approval-gated MCP call (`add_repo`), and on 2026-08-06 that gate returned `MCP error -32003: MCP tool call requires approval` INSTANTLY on every retry while the operator was actively clicking approve — each call errors before the prompt can be answered, so the click always lands on a dead prompt. An earlier `add_repo` in the same session had succeeded, so it is not a static permission: it regressed mid-session, possibly client-specific (the successes were desktop, the failures mobile). Consequence for Front Desk: an item that ranks top and reads `fits: true` is still unworkable if its repo was not scoped at creation — the `fits` predicate reports capabilities, not repo scope. Workarounds in order: scope at creation (removes the need to CALL add_repo — see the next caveat, it does not disarm the gate); approve from desktop/web rather than mobile; and note a public repo stays read-clonable through the git proxy with NO attach, so evidence-gathering works even when acting does not. Tracked as front-desk-scheduler#159; the fix itself is Anthropic's.

SCOPING AT CREATION DOES NOT DISARM THE -32003 GATE — it only removes your dependence on `add_repo`, which is one caller of it. Measured 2026-08-06 in a session that WAS correctly scoped at creation (six repos in the dialog, add_repo never called): `send_later` returned -32003 three and a half hours AFTER the same call had succeeded in that same session. No repo scope was involved. So the gate degrades for approval-gated MCP calls as a class. Two consequences for a long session: a workaround verified at session start is not verified for the session (the #119 shape — a defect that only exists BETWEEN runs cannot be caught by testing one run — pointed at the harness rather than a projector); and anything scheduled for later should not go through that gate. `CronCreate` is harness-native rather than an approval-gated MCP call and worked when send_later would not, but the tradeoff is real: a CronCreate job is session-only and in-memory so it dies with the session, where send_later survives a container restart. Never retry a -32003 — each retry mints a fresh prompt whose call has already errored.

A workflow_dispatch 403 from the session SHELL is not the ticket window being shut (measured 2026-08-06). `curl -X POST .../workflows/claim-ticket.yml/dispatches` with the ambient proxy-injected token returns 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'; `mcp__github__actions_run_trigger` on the SAME workflow in the same session returns 204, and the FDS-CLAIM-RESULT verdict reads back through get_job_logs within the minute. proposals/broker-session-tier/ cites the 403 as evidence the window is costly to reach — right about the VERB (a Node script has no gh, 403s from curl, and cannot invoke the agent's MCP tools), wrong about the WINDOW. Same sentinel fact as always: borrow an identity that holds a credential; the MCP server is one, the shell is not.

The session's ambient GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN is proxy-local: git operations work through the session's git proxy, but the token is NOT valid against api.github.com, so worker/lease refuses claim-plane WRITES from a session (403: neither a valid user token nor an installation token — verified 2026-07-30 via src/lease-client.ts against the deployed worker). Writes belong to CI (github.token is an installation token; production-a2 green at 16 and 32 agents same day) or to a real token via FDS_CLAIM_TOKEN — which is a secret, so it never goes in environmentVariables (first caveat). The unauthenticated READ surface (/history, /status) works fine from sessions.
